rawFindings.title: Semicolons before ++/-- are no longer reported in never mode
rawFindings.explanation: The new pattern matches `+` or `-` anywhere in the next token, so `++` and `--` are treated as opt-out tokens. In `semi: ["never"]`, `isUnnecessarySemicolon` then returns false for a semicolon followed by a prefix update on the next line, leaving an extra semicolon unreported even though removing it is safe and was previously enforced.
rawFindings.suggestion: Anchor the opt-out pattern to single-character tokens, e.g. restore `/^[-[(\/+]$/` or use `/^(?:[[(\/]|[+-])$/`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: With rule options `["never"]`, input `a;\n++b` produces no error, but it should report and fix the extra semicolon to `a\n++b`.
